findings.summary: CLI crashes on --help and --version when API keys are not configured, because importing getResponse triggers module-level env var checks in config.ts before commander parses arguments
findings.failure_scenario: User runs 'deepresearch --help' without setting JINA_API_KEY env var. Import chain cli.ts -> agent.ts -> config.ts executes line 137 'if (!JINA_API_KEY) throw new Error("JINA_API_KEY not found")' at module load time, crashing before commander outputs help text.

findings.summary: 'main' field 'dist/index.js' points to a file that will never exist: no src/index.ts source file means tsc never creates dist/index.js, making the package unimportable
findings.failure_scenario: User runs 'npm install node-deepresearch' followed by 'require("node-deepresearch")' or 'import ... from "node-deepresearch"'. Node resolves to dist/index.js which does not exist, producing MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The package also has no 'bin' field, so the CLI command cannot be invoked either.

findings.summary: When evaluator deems answer definitive but references are missing and URLs are available, the code still sets isAnswered=true and breaks out of the loop, returning an unreferenced answer (pre-existing bug now exposed through the new CLI)
findings.failure_scenario: Agent produces an answer the evaluator accepts (is_definitive=true) but without references. The condition on line 389 'thisStep.references?.length > 0 || Object.keys(allURLs).length === 0' is false (references.length is 0 and URLs exist). The else branch pushes a diary note about needing references, but execution falls through to line 421 'isAnswered = true; break', exiting the loop and returning the unreferenced answer. The agent should continue searching for references instead.

findings.summary: parseInt(val) validation accepts inputs like '10abc' (returns 10) and '0x10' (returns 16), silently coercing garbage suffixes into numbers
findings.failure_scenario: User runs 'deepresearch -t 50abc "query"' expecting an error for the invalid number. parseInt('50abc') returns 50, so the token budget is silently set to 50 instead of the intended 500000 or producing a validation error. Use Number(val) or val.match(/^\d+$/) for strict validation.

findings.summary: jest.mock('../agent', ...) is dead code: all tests use execAsync which spawns child processes where the mock has no effect, and no test imports the mocked module directly
findings.failure_scenario: A developer adds tests that call getResponse directly (not through execAsync), expecting the mock to intercept them. The mock is silently non-functional for the existing test pattern, and the tests pass only because real environment variables satisfy the module-load checks. If a future test relies on the mock, it will call the real agent with real API costs.

findings.summary: GOOGLE_API_KEY env var is set from secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY (wrong secret name); the codebase never reads GOOGLE_API_KEY and always passes GEMINI_API_KEY explicitly to createGoogleGenerativeAI, making this mapping dead and misleading
findings.failure_scenario: If future code changes rely on GOOGLE_API_KEY env var (e.g., using @ai-sdk/google's default credential resolution), it would silently receive the Gemini API key instead of a dedicated Google API key, potentially causing auth failures for non-Gemini Google services. Currently the mapping is harmless dead config copied from the existing test.yml.

findings.summary: @types/commander ^2.12.0 is installed alongside commander ^13.1.0; commander v13 ships its own TypeScript types, and the v2 type definitions are for a completely different API surface, risking type conflicts
findings.failure_scenario: TypeScript may resolve @types/commander's module declaration for 'commander' instead of commander v13's built-in types. The code currently works around this by typing options as 'any', but if someone adds typed option access, they would get v2-era types that don't match the v13 API (e.g., missing features, different method signatures).
